project.name: EndlessSketch
project.summary: Windows deep-zoom drawing application with effectively unbounded hierarchical coordinates, durable vector operations, and rebuildable PNG LOD tiles.

main_goals.goal: Maintain a data-safe, responsive drawing workflow across arbitrary practical distances and depth levels.

architecture.style: Rust desktop application with a GPU UI, normalized hierarchical camera, persistent operation log, spatial tile index, background raster cache, and verified recovery checkpoints.
layers: BigInt hierarchical coordinates and depth-normalized camera
Brush, eraser, lasso fill, eyedropper, bookmarks, and persistent undo/redo
SQLite/WAL vector source data and rotating verified backups
Spatially filtered asynchronous 512px PNG tile cache
notes: Documents use a directory-based .esketch format; PNG tiles are rebuildable and never replace vector source operations.
Content revisions are monotonic and persisted in SQLite so a stale tile cannot become current after restart.
The current local branch is test and remains six commits behind origin/test; no pull, commit, or push was performed.
Existing untracked .idea, .ess, and .esp files are user-owned and must not be changed or committed without an explicit request.

rules.rule: System, developer, and direct user instructions take precedence over this project-local status file.
Higher numeric priority means stronger project-local precedence.
Read this status file before starting project work and update request_analysis before behavior-changing code edits.
After every completed plan item, persist the result and next action in status_worker.json and docs/project-implementation-plan.md, then start the next item from those files as fresh working context.

Keep each task deliberately short and bounded. Split larger work into smaller checkpoints so the user can test and redirect during implementation; avoid bundling multiple interaction changes in one uninterrupted pass.
Do not modify or commit user-owned untracked files unless the user explicitly places them in scope.
Vector operations and SQLite metadata are authoritative; caches must always be safe to delete and rebuild.
Run cargo fmt, Clippy with warnings denied, relevant tests, and a release build after behavior, interface, dependency, or persistence changes.
Keep documentation aligned when behavior, commands, setup, or user workflows change.
